company_name: Deep Source Holdings Limited (formerly Theme International Holdings)

inputs.base_revenue_basis: FY2025 Distribution, trading and processing segment revenue ONLY (0990.HK_Annual_FY2025.txt:6551). The continuing financial-services segment (HK$847.5m FY2025 / HK$423.5m H1 FY2026) is excluded from the flows: it is dominated by a consolidated Singapore fund vehicle (Theme International VCC, 68% held by outside investors, note 40) whose income leaks to NCI, plus money-lending and fund-management fees that are immaterial. Its net assets are inside the cash/financial-asset bridge items and its outside investors inside the NCI deduction.
inputs.share_count_basis: 14,801,345,000 ordinary shares in issue at 30 June 2026 (interim note 19, after the 515m-share placement completed 13 Feb 2026). Basic = diluted per the interim EPS note; no options, warrants or convertibles. Held flat: no SBC scheme exists, and no further placement is announced.
inputs.net_debt_basis: 30 June 2026 balance sheet, CONTINUING operations only (held-for-sale brokerage excluded). Cash HK$3,725.7m less restricted deposits of HK$659.5m pledged against bills payable (interim MD&A 'Charges in Assets') = HK$3,066.2m. Debt = trust receipt loans 283.9 + bank borrowings 521.9 current + 0.8 non-current + lease liabilities 8.8 + 4.0 = HK$819.4m (interim balance sheet lines 337-354; financial-parser's extractor missed the trust-receipt/bank-borrowing labels, so these were read off the statement directly). Brokerage client money (HK$5.0bn) sits in assets held for sale and is excluded.
inputs.reported_fcf_basis: The statutory FY2025 FCF of HK$1,556.4m (OCF 1,563.2 less capex 6.7) is unusable as a base: group OCF is dominated by brokerage client-money, margin and derivative flows and by working-capital swings on a HK$20-55bn trading book (OCF was HK$7.5bn on HK$11bn revenue in FY2019). `reported_fcf` here is the component-built FY2025 trading-segment cash earnings BEFORE stripping interest income: segment profit 490.5 + D&A 34.9 - corporate costs 18.7 = EBITDA 506.8; less D&A = EBIT 471.9; x (1-18%) = 387.0; + D&A 34.9 - capex 6.7 = 415.2 ex working capital; + interest income 116.3 = 531.3. `last_fcf` = 531.3 - 0 SBC - 116.3 interest income = 415.0.
inputs.sbc_source: No share-based payment expense in the FY2025 cash-flow reconciliation or the equity note; no share option scheme grants outstanding. SBC-zero market: rows kept explicit at 0%, house and street bases coincide, band_position null.
inputs.wacc_rationale: HKD flows discounted at an HKD-built cost of equity: HKD risk-free ~3.8% (HKD is pegged to USD; 10y Exchange Fund Note tracks the UST 10y), equity risk premium 6.0%, beta 1.2 for a sub-scale, thin-margin bulk-commodity trader = 11.0%. Debt is <10% of capital so WACC ~ cost of equity; rounded to 11%. Governance history (2024 Singapore misappropriation), related-party concentration and the unproven lithium/AI pivot are charged in the scenario weights and the bear path, NOT as a further WACC premium, and the same WACC is used in all three scenarios (risk charged once).
inputs.lease_treatment: (A) leases as debt: lease liabilities (HK$12.8m) included in total_debt; lease principal NOT deducted from the flows; right-of-use depreciation is inside da_pct_path and renewal inside capex_pct_path. Leases are immaterial (<0.1% of revenue).
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI charged once, in the bridge: the full HK$1,164.1m NCI book at 30 June 2026 is deducted. It comprises ~HK$766m of outside investors in the consolidated Theme International VCC fund (68% NCI, book ~ fair value for a fund), the 23.5% outside stake in BPI Financial Group (the brokerage being sold to Marex, so their claim on the proceeds is covered here), and 40% of a small PRC mining sub. The trading subsidiaries in the flows (King Topwell, Deep Source Pte) are 100%-owned, so the flows carry no NCI leakage. Deducting NCI at book over-charges by ~HK$85m relative to the NCI's share of the HK$1,304m consideration (23.5% x the HK$1,663m carrying value of the disposal group vs 23.5% x 1,304) - accepted as conservative.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (engine route) on the CONTINUING distribution/trading/processing segment, plus a sum-of-parts equity bridge, per SKILL.md's 'straddles two rows: value the parts and sum' rule. Routing: the trading business is an operating company (owner-FCF + adaptations: HKD WACC, leases, NCI, matching-asset rule, SBC-zero); the brokerage is a live trade sale (deal-completes vs deal-breaks) carried as a bridge item rather than projected; the associates and the consolidated fund are passive holdings carried at value in the bridge with their income excluded from the flows. The lithium/AI pivot is NOT in the base-case flows: it has no disclosed capex, partners or timeline, and the only committed step (the US$70m Tortuga de Oro purchase from Tibet Summit Resources, agreed 24 April 2026) is held at cost (cash out = asset in, net zero) in base; the bear case writes it and a further year of pivot spending off through capex. First valuation of this ticker; no memory entry.

equity_bridge.item: Interest in associates at 75% of book (income excluded from flows)
equity_bridge.note: Carrying value HK$2,771.5m at 30 June 2026 (interim balance sheet line 297): Green Esteel, Lianyungang Hengxintong Mining, Shandong Energy Ronghui - equity-accounted iron-ore/steel traders, several related to the controlling shareholder. Share of profits (FY2025 HK$200.4m, H1 FY2026 HK$134.5m) is stripped from the flows under the matching-asset rule and the asset added here. 25% haircut to book for poor cash conversion (dividends received HK$6.8m FY2025 vs HK$200m profit share), related-party governance and no observable market.

equity_bridge.item: Financial assets at FVTPL/FVTOCI at book
equity_bridge.note: Non-current FVTOCI 21.3 + FVTPL 149.3; current FVTPL 276.8 + FVTOCI 0.7 (30 June 2026). Largely the consolidated fund's portfolio; its outside investors are inside the NCI deduction. Net derivative position (assets 1,222.5 vs liabilities 1,317.8) is trading-book hedging and left inside working capital.

equity_bridge.item: Marex disposal proceeds for BPI brokerage entities, time- and formula-discounted
equity_bridge.note: SP Agreement 9 July 2026: consideration estimated at ~HK$1,304m on the Target Group's May-2026 tangible NAV, subject to formula adjustment, completion expected within 12 months (interim note 6). Carried at 1,304 x 0.92 ~ 1,200 for ~9 months to completion at the WACC and the formula risk. Deal-breaks downside is limited: the group would keep a brokerage with HK$1,663m consolidated carrying net assets earning HK$150-200m/yr pre-tax. The NCI's 23.5% claim on these proceeds is inside the NCI deduction below. Bermuda/HK: no capital-gains tax on the disposal.
See inputs.nci_treatment. Fund outside-investors ~766m + BPI 23.5% minority + PRC mining 40% minority.

equity_bridge.item: Tortuga de Oro lithium acquisition (US$70m / HK$546m, agreed 24 Apr 2026) - held at cost
equity_bridge.note: Not completed at 30 June 2026; cash is still in the net-cash figure. Base case: asset credited at cost, so net zero. Bear case charges the HK$546m plus a further HK$250m of pivot spending through capex_pct_path in Y1-Y2 at zero return. Bull case credits nothing beyond cost either; the upside is left as unmodelled optionality.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: long-run trading-volume growth ~ nominal GDP after the FY2026 iron-ore surge unwinds; neither the equity CAGR (inflated by HK$762m of placements and the FY2021-23 super-cycle retained earnings) nor the revenue CAGR (precious-metal ingot trading started and stopped) is a usable forward proxy for a commodity trader
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR +16.9% vs revenue -18.3% and EPS -16.7%: book value compounded on retained super-cycle profits and two equity placements while revenue and EPS fell by half. For a trader, revenue is volume x price and carries no information about value; segment profit is the series that matters.
historical_growth.notes: fcf_3yr_cagr is the FY2022->FY2025 CAGR of trading-segment profit (1,224.3 -> 490.5), the only owner-FCF-like series that is clean of brokerage client-money flows; fcf_5yr_cagr is FY2020->FY2025 (442.9 -> 490.5, 0990.HK_Annual_FY2020.txt:4190): the super-cycle came and went inside the window. Reported FCF (FY2020 6,177 -> FY2025 1,556) is meaningless for this company - see inputs.reported_fcf_basis.

base.growth_note: Y1 = FY2026: H1 trading revenue HK$14,540m (+49% YoY on iron-ore volumes); H2 assumed ~HK$12,460m for FY2026 ~HK$27,000m (+31.7%). Y2 gives back 8% as volumes normalise; thereafter 3% tapering to 2.5%.
base.margin_note: EBITDA = segment profit + D&A - corporate costs, as % of trading revenue. Segment-profit margin history 2.83 / 3.22 / 1.99 / 0.43 / 2.39 / 2.31% (FY2021-FY2025, H1 FY2026); mean 2.2%. Base holds the through-cycle 2.25% from Y3 (segment ~2.15% + D&A 0.20 - corporate 0.09). Y1 2.40% is H1 FY2026's 2.31% segment margin plus the D&A/corporate adjustment, i.e. NOT extrapolating the strong half upward.
base.tax_note: Cash tax 18%: HK 16.5%, Singapore 17%, PRC 25%, Pillar Two 15% floor; FY2025 effective 14.3% and H1 FY2026 19.2% on PBT ex untaxed associates. No NCI leakage in the flows (trading subsidiaries 100%-owned).
base.wc_note: Net operating working capital (inventories 4,464 + trade/bills receivables 4,881 + prepayments 2,646 - trade/bills payables 8,657 - contract liabilities 1,268 - accruals 632) ~ HK$1.4bn = ~5% of revenue; growth consumes 5% of the revenue increase, decline releases it. Capex Y1 0.9%: H1 FY2026 PPE additions HK$145.4m (processing facility, pledged) annualised; then 0.25-0.3% vs D&A 0.2%.
base.terminal_note: 10x cap on terminal FCF for a thin-margin cyclical trader (owner-fcf.md s.4 says 12-15x for cyclicals; this one is sub-scale with a governance record). Gordon at 11%/2% would be 11.3x so the cap binds slightly.

bull.narrative: FY2026 iron-ore volumes hold into FY2027, the Indonesian nickel/bauxite and Australian offtake/JV initiatives funded by the 2025-26 placements add volume at 5-6% for three years, and margins return to the FY2021-22 band (2.8-2.9% EBITDA) as processing income and the PRC import channel scale. The lithium/AI pivot is still credited at zero beyond cost.

bear.narrative: A FY2024-type year recurs: H2 FY2026 softens (Y1 margin 2.2%), FY2027 volumes fall 30% and margin collapses to 1.0% on a Chinese steel downturn and a counterparty default (FY2024 was 0.43%; FY2025 booked a HK$61m client default), recovering only to 1.8% - below the through-cycle mean - as related-party deal flow thins. The pivot destroys capital: the HK$546m Tortuga de Oro purchase plus a further ~HK$250m of lithium/AI spending go through capex in Y1-Y2 at zero return (capex 2.9% / 1.6%).

scenario_narratives.base: Deep Source after the Marex sale is a HK$20-30bn-revenue iron-ore, nickel/chrome-ore and steel trader earning a through-cycle ~2.2% segment margin, plus a HK$2.8bn book of equity-accounted steel-trading associates and ~HK$2.2bn of net cash. FY2026 is a strong volume year (H1 revenue +49%) that the base lets partially unwind in FY2027, then grows at ~3% with margins held at the six-period mean rather than the H1 FY2026 print. The brokerage proceeds and the associates are bridge items, not growth drivers; the lithium/AI transformation is carried at the cost of what has actually been committed (Tortuga de Oro) and nothing more.
scenario_narratives.bull: Volumes from the funded Indonesian and Australian initiatives compound at 5-6% for three years and margins recover to the FY2021-22 band (2.8-2.9%). Even here the pivot is credited at zero beyond cost - a successful lithium-chain build-out is upside to the bull, not inside it.
scenario_narratives.bear: Trading reverts to FY2024 economics for two years (margin 1.0-1.4%, revenue -30%) and settles below the through-cycle mean; the pivot consumes ~HK$800m at zero return. The associates and net cash still underpin the value, which is why the bear case does not collapse: most of this company's value is on the balance sheet, not in the trading P&L.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 30% from the 15% house default: the thesis rests on an unproven, unfunded pivot run by a controlling shareholder with a 2024 misappropriation incident in a subsidiary and heavy related-party dealing, and the trading P&L has already shown a near-zero-margin year (FY2024). Bull cut to 20% because it needs several independent things to go right (sustained iron-ore volumes, Indonesian/Australian ramp, margin recovery). The Marex deal is not a scenario axis: the deal-breaks downside is small because the retained brokerage would be worth roughly its HK$1.3-1.7bn net assets anyway.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value what exists, not what is promised. The continuing trading business is capitalised on through-cycle margins at a 10x terminal cap; the balance sheet (net cash, associates at a haircut, the brokerage sale proceeds, net of minorities) is added once, with every stripped income stream matched to its asset. The lithium/AI pivot is carried at committed cost only. At the current price the market is paying roughly book value, i.e. roughly the bridge plus a modest trading franchise.
key_risks_to_valuation: Associates carried at 75% of a HK$2.77bn book with almost no dividend history; a further haircut of 25pp is ~HK$0.05/share
Net cash of HK$2.2bn is partly working-capital float for a HK$30bn trading book and may not be fully distributable; trade-finance banks already hold HK$659m as restricted deposits (excluded)
Marex consideration is formula-based on tangible NAV and not final; 23.5% of it belongs to BPI minorities
Pivot capital allocation: US$70m Tortuga de Oro is the first of what could be several lithium/AI deals with no disclosed return framework
FY2024 shows the trading margin can go to ~0.4% in a bad year; the model's 2.25% through-cycle margin is the single most sensitive driver
Governance: 2024 Singapore subsidiary misappropriation (HK$167m), related-party trading and financing, no internal audit function in FY2025
